sjoberg-2013-maintenance.citation: Dag I.K. Sjoberg, Aiko Yamashita, Bente C.D. Anda, et al.. Quantifying the Effect of Code Smells on Maintenance Effort (IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering, vol 39 no 8, 1144-1156, 2013)
sjoberg-2013-maintenance.dataset_artifact_revision: Author-hosted preprint accessed 2026-09-08; PDF SHA-256 bce67dea23fb44051c18a4ace609ae09229664e7a40ff075e62280d5ba29b66c (866532 bytes). No study dataset imported. Journal DOI/version retained separately.
sjoberg-2013-maintenance.dataset_artifact_license: Author-hosted reading copy; IEEE copyright notice. No dataset or redistribution license inferred.
sjoberg-2013-maintenance.studied_population: Six professional developers selected from a 65-person pool; three adaptive/perfective maintenance tasks on four independently implemented, functionally equivalent Java web systems. Eleven completed developer-system combinations; 298 distinct modified Java files.
sjoberg-2013-maintenance.comparison_baseline: Nested file-level log-linear models: developer/system/round; add 12 tool-defined smells; add file size; add revisions as a quality proxy. No randomized cleaned-versus-original intervention.
sjoberg-2013-maintenance.relevant_sections: Full author manuscript pp. 1-15: sections 1-7, Tables 1-9 and appendix. Model 3 adjusted R2=0.58 with or without smell predictors; section 5.1 explicitly distinguishes God Class/Method from unmeasured Large Class/Long Method.
sjoberg-2013-maintenance.threats: Small selected professional sample; four small Java web systems; one unfinished developer-system round excluded; tool-specific smell definitions; file-level effort can miss cross-file/method-level effects; first major maintenance may miss long-term effects. Revisions are a quality proxy, not direct defects. No universal harmlessness or causal benefit from reducing size follows.

buse-2010-readability.citation: Raymond P. L. Buse, Westley R. Weimer. Learning a Metric for Code Readability (IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering, vol 36 no 4, 546-558, 2010)
buse-2010-readability.dataset_artifact_revision: Author-linked 14-page TSE preprint accessed 2026-09-08; PDF SHA-256 7eb4313d2a3d2f090de5eab362970b9ac69b7da205b8dac32f7d299a6644fac9 (1635323 bytes). No training data or model imported. Reader TLS validation failed; browser confirmed author link and curl --insecure retrieved it. This identifies the reading copy, not publisher byte identity.
buse-2010-readability.dataset_artifact_license: Author-linked reading copy; no dataset/model redistribution license inferred.
buse-2010-readability.studied_population: 120 University of Virginia CS students (17 first-year, 63 second-year, 30 third/fourth-year, 10 graduate) judged the same 100 short Java snippets from five projects; 12000 rating opportunities, 15 skipped. External correlations on 15 Java projects; 12 had sufficient version-control history.
buse-2010-readability.comparison_baseline: Random-label classifiers and annotator-versus-average agreement; repeated 10-fold snippet cross-validation (10 repetitions). External correlations with FindBugs, version changes, bug-mentioning commits, maturity and cyclomatic complexity, not randomized readability improvements.
buse-2010-readability.relevant_sections: Full 14-page preprint sections 1-9, Figures 1-15 and references. Sections 2-4: survey, feature extraction, threshold 3.14, repeated cross-validation; sections 5-7: external correlations, descriptive-not-prescriptive warning and validity limits.
buse-2010-readability.threats: Single-institution mostly undergraduate Java judgment sample; local snippets deliberately omit wider context; same snippet order, unguided subjective scoring, and source-project overlap do not establish project-held-out transfer. Bug mentions/FindBugs/churn are proxies. Section 6 explicitly rejects treating descriptive feature associations as prescriptive edits; not a Rust/Python or maintenance-benefit validation.

source_review.scope: Both requested primary-text blockers resolved; not dataset import or independent deslop validation. Paper plots not independently digitized.
